subject: Feature retention while moving to Compact tier - CareDock
messages:
From: Miguel Torres <miguel@caredock.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: CareDock Procurement <procurement@caredock.ai>, Sophie Leung <sophie.leung@caredock.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Moving to Compact tier but need to retain Private VPC + Audit logs

Hey Stephanie —

Quick question on packaging before our renewal call: we’re planning to move most workloads to the Compact tier to save costs, but two features are must-haves for our compliance team: Private VPC and HIPAA-grade audit logs / retention (the ones we marked as "protected" in the feature list).

Can you confirm:
- Whether those features can be retained on Compact (either as add-ons or an exception).
- If retained, what the charge would be (monthly fixed or per-token uplift).
- How step-down credits/commit proration would work if we reduce committed throughput mid-term.

I attached a short list of the features we need and our procurement notes.

Thanks — Miguel
Miguel Torres
Head of Platform, CareDock
[Attachment: CareDock_Requested_Features_20280814.pdf (pdf)]
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Torres <miguel@caredock.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Moving to Compact tier but need to retain Private VPC + Audit logs

Miguel —

Thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. Short answer: yes, we can keep those two features while moving to Compact, but there are two common approaches and trade-offs:

1) Compact + Protected Feature Add-on
   - Private VPC and Audit Log retention are sold as named add-ons.
   - Pricing: a fixed monthly addon fee + small per-token storage charge for long retention windows.
   - Pros: simplest operationally, no change to contract topology.
   - Cons: add-on not covered by committed throughput; will show as separate line item.

2) Exception/Hybrid Pack (temporary)
   - We create a hybrid commitment that keeps Compact compute pricing but pins a small Dedicated-like allocation for the protected features (isolation and throughput guarantees).
   - Pricing: modest uplift to the commit-level for the duration of the exception.
   - Pros: predictable unit economics and easier SLOs for the features.
   - Cons: requires approval from Sales Ops for a custom pricing line.

On proration/step-down credits: if you reduce committed throughput mid-term, we typically prorate committed credits; add-ons are prorated independently. If you take option (2) we can negotiate a gentler step-down (longer tail) because the hybrid carve-out requires capacity planning.

Can we hop on a 30-min call tomorrow to map which option you prefer and I’ll loop in Ben (pricing) and Lauren (contract/cash ops) to model numbers? If useful I can draft the exception term and share a DocuSign link for approval.

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Torres <miguel@caredock.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Moving to Compact tier but need to retain Private VPC + Audit logs

Miguel — looping in a couple of technical/ops notes so expectations are set:

- Private VPC: operationally we can route traffic from Compact model endpoints through a customer-managed VPC peering. There’s a one-time setup fee and a small monthly isolation charge if we reserve subnets for you.

- Audit logs + retention: long retention (>=1 year) has storage and egress costs. We usually model this as: base addon $1,200/mo + $0.15/GB/mo for stored logs beyond 90 days.

- Hybrid approach: if you want guaranteed throughput for protected workloads, we need to reserve a tiny Dedicated pool (we can size it conservatively). That affects committed throughput math and can reduce token overages.

I put estimated numbers in the attached stub; Dev — can you confirm the minimum Dedicated slice we’d need for the audit pipeline if CareDock wants sub-50ms tail latency on audit writes?

[Attachment: protected-features-exception-term.docx (docx)]

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Moving to Compact tier but need to retain Private VPC + Audit logs

Team —

Thanks for the call earlier. Summary and next steps:

- Path chosen: Compact tier + Protected Feature Add-on (Option 1) with a 6-month review. We will not provision a Dedicated slice for now.
- Pricing agreed (preliminary): $1,200/mo add-on + $0.12/GB/mo for retained audit logs (first 90 days included).
- Step-down: if CareDock reduces committed throughput during the 6-month window we’ll prorate the commit and keep the add-on billing aligned month-to-month. No step-down credits for the add-on itself.
- Documentation: I uploaded the exception term and the one-page summary to HubSpot and created a DocuSign envelope. Please review and sign: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/DEAL-4729 and https://redwood.app/docusign/ABC-7392.

Action items:
- CareDock procurement to sign exception term by Aug 22 (Sophie).
- Dev/Ben to validate audit-write latency using the test harness in sandbox account (Dev).
- Stephanie & Lauren to process updated quote and send amended invoice upon signature.

If anything needs to change we can escalate to Sales Ops, but this should let you move most workloads to Compact and keep the compliance posture you need.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

—Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
